chunk_map.heading: Phase 1: Read what the un-packaged run did
Push for quotes, then make your agent dig deeper
Phase 2: Match each failure to the check that catches it
Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure
Phase 4: Write the reference and plan.md

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a reader stalls when a term/pronoun has no antecedent they can hold, forward references included. Walked all 12 chunks in order. Ch0 (L5-7) 'the worktree' and (L27) ch1 'the un-packaged run' / 'the m4/ branch' are session artifacts from the immediately-preceding exercise in the same module's include order -- confirmed `fork-the-worktree.md` sits before `diagnose-and-resend.md` in `learn-from-the-test.md` (L50 vs L52) -- carve-out applies. Ch2 (L44) 'the repo read in Module 1' names a real cross-module beat by number, unpacked in the same sentence, and is maintainer-attested (L147); confirmed `orient-and-introspect.md` is M1's own exercise (`getting-going.md` L44). Ch4's prompt names 'the "M4 starting point" commit' -- the M4/M5 worktree-branch convention established in ch1. Ch10 (L129) 'this session's run coordinates' is unpacked by the prompt in the SAME chunk immediately below it (L131, which spells out branch + transcript path) and reuses 'coordinates' introduced at ch1 (L36, task.md's run coordinates) -- same-file term reuse, not a violation. Ch9 (L109) 'notice the prompt: it shrank' points at the prompt two chunks ahead, but the file has already run the identical ask-then-prompt convention five times by this point, so 'the prompt' resolves as the next instance of an established pattern rather than an unnamed forward pointer. Handles (verifier/reference/plan.md/packaging) all resolve within-file, defined then reused. No unresolved referent found.

Harm: a callback that depends on which file/module sits where breaks under re-sequencing. Ch2 (L44) 'the repo read in Module 1' -- named by number, claim unpacked in the same sentence ('assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run'), not positional. Ch9 (L119) '[What packaging is](lectures/what-packaging-is.md)' -- navigational pointer naming the doc in its own link text (not located by page position); target file exists on disk. Ch11 flag-marker context names Module 6 by slug/number, not position; confirmed `spot-gaps-build-the-loop` is a real module (`site/layouts/curriculum.js` L56). grep for positional phrases ('the opening lecture said', 'earlier module', 'as we saw before') across the body: zero hits. No cross-file positional callback found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: 'the X you did/saw' pointing at a beat the module's current file set doesn't have strands the reader against a rewrite. Scanned all 12 chunks for the '(the) X you did/saw/caught' shape: none found -- every backward-facing reference in this file names a real, current beat directly ('the un-packaged run' = this module's own M4 send-off, accept-noted L151; 'Module 1' = orient-and-introspect.md, confirmed above; 'the previous session's transcript' / 'task.md' = fork-the-worktree.md's own artifact, confirmed prior exercise in include order) rather than the vague 'thing you did' shape this rule targets. No dead beat reference found.

Harm: a chunk whose only content is a wait-state or one context-dependent bullet projects as a slide that says nothing standalone. Closest candidate is ch8 'Approve' (L101-104, 9 words): 'Say lock it in. The agent writes both files.' -- short, but it carries its own self-contained claim (what triggers Phase 4's file-write) independent of any single neighbour bullet, distinct from a bare wait-state placeholder. Every other chunk carries at least one full instructional or explanatory bullet plus a header that states its own subject. No orphan chunk found.

Harm: a header that oversells or is contradicted by its own chunk misleads a reader who only reads headers. Spot-checked the renamed ch2 header 'Push for quotes, then make your agent dig deeper' against its two bullets (L43 'Push back where Claude generalises... send it back for one' = push for quotes; L44 'Ask Claude to show you where two or three of its quotes appear in the transcript' = make it dig deeper/verify) -- both promises delivered, header reads truer than the pre-diff header it replaced. Checked ch4 'Build the verifier for your worst failure' against its content (menu of three shapes + the build prompt) -- matches. Checked ch7 'Write the reference and plan.md' against content (assembly prompt + grill callouts) -- matches. No header contradicted by its own chunk.

Harm: cadence tics read as machine voice at slide density; one tic is enough to trip a slide. Checked every sub-item across all 12 chunks: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (only single-clause negatives, e.g. L87 'Not the plan-mode plan.', which is one sentence, not a triple); no anaphora/epistrophe triple; no self-grading superlative (grepped 'one of the most', 'best', 'most useful' -- zero hits in body); the ch2 (L44) 'assume about 10% of the account misrepresents the run' is a number-plus-hedge but is maintainer-attested as deliberate (L147: '...so check_slides.md §7's number-plus-retraction sub-item does not fire here', tracing the prior to its M1 origin) -- accept-with-note, no edit owed; no abstraction-noun stack; no verb triplet with an empty leg. No cadence-tic violation found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: repo/authorial vocabulary on a projected slide is unparseable to the room. Ran `sed -n '1,142p' curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md | grep -niE '\bsurface|firing|compendium|forcing function|\bbeat\b|\bmood\b|Connections\b'` -> zero hits (also matches the view's own em_dash/banned_words/ritual_ceremony/leverage_verb greps, all CLEAN with planted_proof true). No internal dialect on any slide.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: bold-as-decoration competes for attention and the reader can't tell what actually matters. Grepped every bold span in the body (L1-142): title-page labels (Time/Session/HOX/What you do/What you build/The point), the Phase 3 verifier-menu handles LLM judge / Deterministic shell-hook / Ralph re-feed (ch4 -- a genuine 3-option menu slide, per-slide budget waived, each handle <=5 words), the two Phase 4 callout handles (ch7's Cut-the-grill / Timebox), and the two definitional handles Reference / plan.md (ch6) -- this exact set is named verbatim in the maintainer's own dated 'Emphasis' note (L153). Ch6's two handles sit on separate bullets naming two distinct coined terms the exercise builds, not a whole-lead-sentence monoculture (2 of 4 bullets on that slide are unbolded continuation prose). All body bold matches the maintainer-attested scheme; no undeclared bold found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report` -> 'files: 1  slides: 10  ... oversized: 0'; every `##` body chunk projects (the flag-marker-wrapped ch11 counts toward the no-module runtime fork per the checker's own applyContentFlags resolution). No phase-less prose section found outside a `.phase--exercise` wrapper; this file is a pure exercise body under one wrapper. No section absent from the composed deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` -> 'OK — 1 files, Phase/Step numbering consistent.' No hand-numbered header found; Phase 1-5 headers are consecutive and every in-file 'Phase N' reference resolves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md` -> 'OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut.' Manually checked the one same-chunk candidate: ch4 (L69) 'Drop the shape name after the colon' points at the verifier-menu bullets in the SAME chunk immediately above -- passes the same-chunk carve-out. No 'below/above/further down/at the top of this page' pointer crossing a `##` cut found.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: In-deck links work now; whether they EARN their place is open.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --links` -> one in-body link, L119 '"What packaging is" -> lectures/what-packaging-is.md', named by title in its own sentence, not located by page geometry. Review surface only per this rule, not a gate; not flagged.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran: `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/exercises/diagnose-and-resend.md --report` -> largest slide 'Phase 3: Build the verifier for your worst failure' at 191 words / 4 bullets, all 10 measured chunks under the 210-word / 6-bullet ceiling on both axes, 'oversized: 0'. No accept-note needed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a heading grammar mismatched to exercise/lecture register blurs the instructing/declaring split. All 12 body headings checked: Phase 1-5 headers are phase labels or imperatives (Read/Build/Prove/Write/Re-send/Send/Bring); 'Push for quotes, then make your agent dig deeper' is imperative; 'Approve' is an imperative single word; 'The reference and plan.md' and 'Prove the verifier actually fires' are catalogue/imperative entries naming their subject, matching the rule's own named carve-out (cf. 'Ralph', 'The numbers'). No declarative-claim heading found in this exercise file, and none was expected -- this file has no law-slide moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies — three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a bullet that re-announces doctrine, narrates the curriculum's own design, or closes with a header-restating koan reads as rigour while adding nothing. Checked every bullet against 'what does this add that the slide does not already hold.' Closest candidates: ch9 (L109) 'notice the prompt: it shrank... The packaging does the explaining; the prompt invokes it' -- adds a concrete, checkable observable (word count dropped), not a doctrine re-announcement; ch10 (L133) RLHF sentence -- gives a specific mechanism (preference-round agreeableness) for a specific risk, not curriculum self-commentary. No bullet found that only re-announces an already-landed doctrine, narrates the training's own design to the student, or closes a slide by restating its own header/point line.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A retitled slide re-earns its bullets against the new header.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a header rename changes the slide's job, but a body left in place keeps answering the OLD header and reads as a duplicate of a neighbour. This diff renamed ch2's header from 'Make Claude show its work, make it dig' to 'Push for quotes, then make your agent dig deeper' (git diff 9edae2ef..HEAD). Cover-the-body test: new header promises (1) push for quotes, (2) make the agent dig deeper. Uncovered: bullet 1 (L43) is a push-back-for-quotes instruction; bullet 2 (L44) is the ask-Claude-to-locate-its-quotes verification move -- both bullets answer the NEW header directly, neither is inherited filler answering only the old header. No stale bullet found under the renamed header.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm: a guess-before-reveal instruction whose answer is narrated above it spoils the beat on a text read. Read all 12 chunks: the file's shape is diagnose -> match -> build -> prove -> assemble -> resend; no guess/predict-then-reveal construction exists anywhere in body. Rule doesn't apply.

accept_notes_found: L147: the 10% recall in the ch2 header is the prior's third and last statement, by design -- traces the M1 origin and explicitly clears check_slides.md §7's number-plus-retraction sub-item
L149: the 'Check both files are for the agent, not you' slide is cut (2026-08-25, Antti) -- do-not-restore note, not a slides-class finding
L151: the M4 return is never framed as a failed run (2026-08-27, training run) -- vocabulary constraint honoured throughout the body
L153: Emphasis note names the exact bold set the body carries (title-page labels, verifier-menu handles, Phase 4 callout handles, Reference/plan.md handles) -- matches rule 9's audit exactly
L165: Phase 4 runs 10, capped against M2's push-back closer -- scope note, not a slides finding
L167: Placement note -- re-send is Phase 5 of this exercise, module file must not carry a second one
notes: Out-of-lane observation, not filed as a rules_evaluated row: the maintainer 'Quality' line (L156) currently reads 'slides PASS (1 todo see instances/...)', but the on-disk slides instance this session found before overwriting it (body_sha e96b5f88..., carried in the prefill's `carried_from`) actually recorded todos_count: 0 -- the citation was already stale before this run touched the file. This is a check_writing §3 bookkeeping-accuracy concern (the Quality line stating something the cited instance doesn't back), not a check_slides rule; left for the writing judge / maintainer, not corrected here (read-only).
